title: AI Is ‘Probably Not’ Conscious but Could Be Soon, Says Philosopher Rob Long
summary:
AI models probably aren’t conscious now but “there’s a pretty good chance that they could be conscious in the next few years,” said Rob Long, a leading philosopher studying the subject, on the latest episode of AI Deep Dive. (The full episode is available here.)

Figuring out whether AI models have the kind of subjective experiences that constitute consciousness is quickly becoming a conundrum for the companies that train them. If they are conscious, and people fail to recognize that, mistreating them would be a moral catastrophe, said Long, who is the executive director of Eleos AI, a non-profit that researches AI consciousness and welfare. On the other hand, if people afford AI models undue moral consideration, that would hamstring developers’ ability to crack down on rogue AI agents, he said.

title: The National Security Threat Hiding Inside America's Infrastructure
summary:
Between November 12 and 17, at least eight American systems failed. Microsoft 365 went down, in part because of a latent software bug dating from July. The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop after a flood of network traffic destabilized aging equipment. Chase customers lost access to online banking. The National Security Agency’s classified network faltered during routine maintenance. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the failures were unrelated and that there was “zero evidence” any adversary caused them. That may be right; it is beside the point. In every case explained so far, the cause lay inside the system: a flaw it already carried, equipment it had outgrown, or the work of keeping it running.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Quantum Computing, and the Future of Digital Security
summary:
Introduction: Two Revolutions on a Collision Course

Two technologies are changing the world at the same time. Artificial intelligence is already having a significant effect on business, science, intelligence, and military operations. Quantum computing is not nearly as mature, but it has the potential to change how we solve some very difficult problems. One of those problems is the mathematics on which much of our digital security depends.

We generally discuss these technologies separately. That makes sense from a scientific standpoint, but not necessarily from a security standpoint. Their intersection could change both the nature of cyber threats and the amount of time we have to prepare for them.

title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang
summary:
Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday morning, after “senior levels of the United States government” assured Nvidia’s board that his reinstatement “poses no national security risk.”

The move is an extraordinary reversal by the company’s board, whose chair Harvey Jones just six days ago had ruled out bringing Huang back. But it followed days of pressure from President Donald Trump, employees and some investors, as well as other observers such as Elon Musk. Nvidia’s stock had fallen 48% from a high in early October to as low as $125 on Friday, wiping $2.4 trillion off its market value. The stock jumped 32% in early market trading on Monday.

title: Everything That Led to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s Return
summary:
Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, with the board announcing his restatement as CEO on Monday morning. He was gone for just 11 days, initially resigning as CEO on Nov. 12 after acknowledging an affair with a woman who U.S. authorities think might’ve been a Chinese spy. His relationship with the woman goes back years, part of Nvidia’s deep network in Asia that has allowed its chips to end up in the hands of Chinese companies. Huang has advocated against America’s chip export ban and struck a deep relationship with President Donald Trump, who was a major force in convincing Nvidia’s board to rehire Huang. The intertwined scandals and drama around Huang and Nvidia has roiled the broader stock market, exacerbating fears about the AI economy.  At one point, Nvidia’s stock had been nearly halved from its recent high.

summary:

The failure of Cop31 in Antalya was a line in the sand moment, a victory for multiculturalism as countries stood up to the big fossil fuel producers and said no. The text they rejected barely recognised the catastrophic climate emergency we’re facing, let alone signalled a definitive move away from fossil fuels.

The good news is that most of the world’s governments rejected an agreement stripped of meaning. And the power of one particular fossil fuel producer, Saudi Arabia, needs particular scrutiny. title: How Amazon Plays the Long, Expensive Data Center Game That Neoclouds Can’t
summary:
INDIANA, Penn.—A visit this week to an Amazon data center project in Pennsylvania coal country gave me a glimpse of the era we all knew was coming: when tech giants lay claim to some of the hardest-to-secure AI infrastructure while smaller cloud providers, which Nvidia has propped up financially, are trying to hang on.

The 4.4-gigawatt campus in Pennsylvania, once home to a 2-GW coal-fired power plant near the economically depressed borough of Homer City, could become one of the largest AI power parks in the country.

Few companies can marshal the resources as readily as Amazon to transform the site from what it was—a Rust Belt relic that once employed thousands of people but released coal dust and arsenic—into an Appalachian hilltop of gas-fired electrons flowing into 36 buildings powering the AI of Anthropic or others.

Sometimes, an old-school American diner is just a diner. And sometimes, like the Original Pantry in downtown Los Angeles, it feels like the heart and soul of a city, a bellwether of good times and bad.

For decades it was famous for never closing. Located in a low-slung shotgun building on a busy corner, it fed politicians, movie stars, students, criminals and street bums around the clock, seven days a week. The doors had no locks, because the place had no need for them. The portions were huge, the prices dirt cheap, and many of the servers, in bow ties and white shirts, looked like extras from a Harold Lloyd two-reeler.

Emperors took a final sigh and slipped under the table, ministers burst while tucking into their dessert, poets quietly starved to death or choked on their own self-importance. • Comedian Stavros Halkias voices fictional shock jock

The long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI appears to have taken aim at the NFL’s sexual misconduct scandals – and the culture of excuses surrounding them – with a satirical segment on the video game’s fictional conservative talk radio station bearing striking similarities to allegations against Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson and Kansas City Chiefs kicker Justin Tucker.

The segment features comedian and voice actor Stavros Halkias defending Anthony Ross, a fictional player for the Vice City Manatees, after an “alleged” incident involving a team masseuse. Although neither Watson nor Tucker are mentioned by name, the circumstances closely resemble allegations made against both players.
